title: Conjecture on the sign of the Stolarsky and power-mean difference
statement:
Let $L_\alpha$ denote the Stolarsky mean, let $B_p$ and $B_q$ be power means, and let $\mathcal{R}(B_p,L_\alpha,B_q)$ denote their associated stabilizing mean. Set

$$
q=\frac12(1-p)-2\alpha^2,\qquad p=\pm\sqrt{1+16\alpha^2-16\alpha^4}.
$$

**Sign conjecture.** The inequality

$$
L_\alpha-\mathcal{R}(B_p,L_\alpha,B_q)<0
$$

holds for $\lvert\alpha\rvert<\frac12$.

This statement concerns the sign needed to determine sub- or super-stabilizability of $L_\alpha$ by power means. The source presents it as motivated by numerical experiments; its resolution is not supplied.
source_name: Lenka Mihoković and Mustapha Raïssouli, “Results on comparison and sub/super-stabilizability of some new means”, arXiv:2405.13618 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.13618

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

title: Conjecture on the sign of the Stolarsky and power-mean difference at exceptional parameters
statement:
Let $S_\alpha$ denote the Stolarsky mean, let $B_p$ and $B_q$ be power means, and let $\mathcal{R}(B_p,S_\alpha,B_q)$ denote their associated stabilizing mean. Set

$$
q=\frac12(1-p)+2\alpha^2,
\qquad
p^2=\frac{1-12\alpha^2+112\alpha^4-64\alpha^6}{1+4\alpha^2}.
$$

**Sign conjecture.** At $\lvert\alpha\rvert=\frac12\sqrt{2\pm\sqrt3}$,

$$
S_\alpha-\mathcal{R}(B_p,S_\alpha,B_q)<0.
$$

The claim arises from asymptotic comparison of $S_\alpha$ with the stabilizing mean generated by power means. The source gives no resolution evidence beyond the preceding asymptotic calculation, so the conjecture remains open.
source_name: Lenka Mihoković and Mustapha Raïssouli, “Results on comparison and sub/super-stabilizability of some new means”, arXiv:2405.13618 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.13618

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

title: Conjecture on the sign of the $M_4$ and power-mean difference
statement:
Let $M_4$ be the mean defined in the paper, let $B_p$ and $B_q$ be power means, and let $\mathcal{R}(B_p,M_4,B_q)$ denote their associated stabilizing mean. Set

$$
p=3-2q,\qquad q=\frac12(3\pm\sqrt{21}).
$$

**Sign conjecture.** Then

$$
M_4-\mathcal{R}(B_p,M_4,B_q)>0.
$$

The claim records the positive sign obtained from the asymptotic expansion relevant to stabilizability of $M_4$ by power means. The source provides no resolution evidence, so the conjecture remains open.

title: The parameter-boundary conjecture for the reverse Mittag–Leffler inequality
statement:
Let $E_{\alpha,\beta}$ be the two-parameter Mittag–Leffler function. A **complete Bernstein function** is understood in the standard sense, and consider the global reverse inequality

$$
\left|E_{\alpha,\beta}(z)\right|\ge E_{\alpha,\beta}(\operatorname{Re}z)\qquad\text{for every }z\in\mathbb{C}.
$$

**The parameter-boundary conjecture.** There exists an increasing convex function $f:[2,\infty)\to[3,\infty)$ with $f(2)=3$ such that, for every $\alpha\ge2$,

$$
\left|E_{\alpha,\beta}(z)\right|\ge E_{\alpha,\beta}(\operatorname{Re}z)\ \text{globally}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\log E_{\alpha,\beta}\ \text{is a complete Bernstein function}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\beta\le f(\alpha).
$$

At $\alpha=2$ the corresponding boundary is known to be $f(2)=3$, and the paper gives partial support for extending this description to $\alpha>2$. The conjecture also predicts monotonicity and convexity of the boundary separating the parameter regions.
source_name: Roberto Garrappa, Stefan Gerhold, Marina Popolizio and Thomas Simon, “On some inequalities for the two-parameter Mittag-Leffler function in the complex plane”, arXiv:2410.11852 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.11852
